en.value: Which of the following is incorrect with regard to 'Transition State Theory' of reactions?

options.prompt: The reactants are first converted to an
The activated complex can be isolated and
The activated complex remains in equilibrium
The activated complex has a transient

english.explanation: The transition state theory of reactions suggests that during a chemical reaction, the reactant molecules undergo a transition state as an activated complex. This transition state is a high energy state where the reactant molecules are in the process of forming or breaking bonds. The option (b) is the incorrect statement as it states that the activated complex is highly unstable and has a transient existence. It exists only for a short period of time during the reaction before it either forms products or reverts back to the reactant. So, in short, the activated, complex can't be isolated and characterized because of its transient nature.

Which one of the following conditions would cause the largest deviation from the van der Waal equation for real gases?

english.explanation: A gas which obeys the ideal gas equation, PV = nRT under all conditions of temperature and pressure is known as ideal gas. Ideal gas is a hypothetical concept as there is no gas which obeys ideal gas equation under all conditions of T and P. It visualizes molecules as rigid spheres which are in constant random motion. At high pressures, the repulsive force experienced by molecules are also high so they have considerable intermolecular force existing between them. Temperature is the measure of the randomness is the measure of the randomness of the molecules. At low temperature, molecules would not possess random motion and the volume of the gas is low. This means, at high pressure and low temperature, real gases show larger deviation from the van der Waals equation.

en.value: A process is said to be 'spontaneous' at all temperature when

english.explanation: A spontaneous process refers to a reaction that occur naturally on its own without any external intervention. For a process to be spontaneous at all temperatures, the change in enthalpy (∆H) should be negative indicating that the process releases heat or DSSSB PGT 157 YCT energy. The change in entropy (∆S) should be positive. This means that the system becomes more disorder and random. For a spontaneous reaction, the sign ∆G must be negative as it relates enthalpy, entropy and temperature. ∆G = ∆Η – T∆S When ∆H < 0 and ∆S > 0 ∆G = – x – y ∴ ∆G will be negative. ∵ The process will be spontaneous if ∆G is –ve Thus, the correct answer is option (c).

en.value: Peptization is a process of

english.explanation: Peptization is a process of converting a precipitate, which is a solid that has separated from a solution, into a colloidal dispersion. It involves breaking down the larger particles of the precipitate into smaller particles, dispersing them evenly throughout the solution. This disperson of smaller particles helps to stabilize the colloidal system and prevent the larger particles from settling out. So, peptization is essentially the process of dispersing precipitates into a colloidal solution.

en.value: In silver chloride, the silver ion is displaced from its lattice points to an interstitial position. Such a defect in the crystal is termed as

english.explanation: In silver chloride, the silver ion is displaced from its lattice points to an interstitial position. Such a defect in the crystal is termed as frenkel defect. Frenkel defect is a point defect that occurs in ionic crystals. It happens when a cation moves from its regular lattice site to an interstitial site creating a vacancy at the original site and an interstitial cation at the new site. This defect doesn't affect the overall charge neutrality of the crystal, but it can impact its conductivity and other properties. Frenkel defect is found in AgCl crystal because there is big difference in the size of the anion and cation.

en.value: Which one of the following statements regarding 'viscosity' is correct?

options.prompt: The viscosities of most liquids decrease with
The viscosities of most liquids increase with
The viscosities of liquids as well as gases
The viscosities of liquids as well as gases

english.explanation: When it comes to viscosity, it refers to the resistance of a substance to flow. In general, for most liquids, as the temperature increases, their viscosity decreases. This means that they becomes less resistance to flow and can flow more easily. On the other hand, for gases, as the temperature increases, their viscosity tends to increase. This means that they become more resistant to flow. It's all about how the temperature affects the movement of particles in the substance.
